structured_output.summary: Ownership design is sound for in-guarantee cases; no demonstrated parent-loss or deadline bypass. One fail-open cleanup path in the guardian (ps-probe failure) and one interruption gap in spawn_in_group were found by inspection only; nothing was executed. Several proof gaps remain. Simultaneous parent+guardian loss is out of guarantee and documented. Not both-platform release acceptance.

findings.title: Guardian skips group SIGKILL when ps probe fails (fail-open after parent loss)
findings.body: live_group_members runs ps with timeout=1, check=True. A timeout/non-zero exit raises at line 137 or 151, jumping to except BaseException (176). That handler gates its kill on workload_alive() again (183); the probe fails the same way and SubprocessError is swallowed at 187, so killpg and process.wait are skipped. The guardian then writes pin-release.json (194) and exits. With a live parent, its pin.signal_group fallback rescues the run; if the parent is already lost the workload group survives with no owner. Inferred from code, not executed; a 1s ps timeout is plausible under load/macOS.
findings.recommendation: Send an unconditional killpg(SIGKILL) in the failure path and treat a probe error as 'alive'. Add fault-injection tests where live_group_members raises during parent-loss cleanup.

findings.title: spawn_in_group signal deferral ends before the handle is assigned by the caller
findings.body: defer_launch_signals restores the mask in its finally before spawn_in_group returns; the caller assigns process = spawn_in_group(...) at _docguardian.py:92. A pending SIGINT delivered at context exit raises KeyboardInterrupt before return, leaving process None while the launcher runs in the group. Only the process-is-None SIGKILL fallback (_docguardian.py:178-180) covers it; the run ends as guardian-failure and the direct child is not reaped by the guardian. run() and GroupPin assign inside the with block and are fine.
findings.recommendation: Return/assign the handle inside the deferral scope (e.g. pass a holder or wrap the caller assignment in the with), and add a test that delivers SIGINT at context exit.

findings.title: Interrupt between GroupPin() return and try leaks the pin
findings.body: Lines 238-240 are outside any try/finally; KeyboardInterrupt there skips pin.finish(). Pin self-exits only when the parent dies, so a long-lived parent keeps it and its PID reservation. Narrow window.
findings.recommendation: Move the pin assignment's follow-up statements inside the try whose finally calls pin.finish().

findings.title: Destructive killpg and pin release not gated on pin still holding the PGID after parent loss
findings.body: After parent loss the pin only reserves identity. If it dies (SIGKILL/OOM) init reaps it and the PGID may be recycled; killpg(SIGKILL) at line 179 and main-path signals do not verify the pin. pin-release.json (194) is also written before the final disappearance check, so cleanup-unverified leaves survivors with no retained owner. The invariant is asserted in comments, not enforced.
findings.recommendation: Verify pin liveness before destructive signals and defer pin release until disappearance is observed or retries are exhausted.

findings.title: Launcher only reports OSError as launch-error
findings.body: A ValueError (e.g. NUL in argv) or other exception exits 1 with no launch-error.json, so the run is reported completed instead of guardian-failure.
findings.recommendation: Catch Exception in the launcher and write launch-error.json.
